newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding temporary reserves Monday.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding temporary reserves Monday.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Monday through overnight or multi-day system repurchase agreements, analysts said.

"I'm looking for an overnight system," said Patricia Thrapp, money market economist at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co. "Funds are firm this morning due to pressures related to the first (business) day of the month and also to the settlement date for $23.0 billion in cash management bills."
Marilyn Schaja, money market economist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, said she expected the Fed to add temporary reserves to the banking system through three-day system repurchase agreements.
"There's a large add need and (Federal) funds are tight," she said.

Analysts at MMS International said they, too, expect the Fed to add temporary reserves through system repurchase agreements. They cited upward pressure on the Federal funds rate due to settlement of the $23.0 billion cash management bills.
At 0932 EST/1432 GMT, Federal funds were trading at 5-3/8 percent, above the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.
